adjudicated.jp: 冬子の家は大きい。
adjudicated.en: Touko's house is huge.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 大きすぎて陽光を遮り、一面の闇にしか見えない。
adjudicated.en: So enormously huge that it intercepts the sunlight, and I can't see anything besides silhouetted darkness.
comments: Hmmm... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The house blocks the sunlight and looks like a single expanse of darkness. 'Silhouetted darkness' is contradictory, and the English adds a claim that the narrator can see nothing else.

highlights.text: So enormously huge that it intercepts the sunlight, and I can't see anything besides silhouetted darkness.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は夜目がきくが、なぜかまったく見えない。
adjudicated.en: I have sharp night eyes, but for some reason I absolutely can't see.
comments: According to CCC4015, it's just the inside that's this dark. And us readers can see perfectly fine, can't we? And he used the exact kanji for "darkness" that, in CCX0001, says he can see through. What's perplexing is only the level of blatancy in this troll. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 夜目がきく means to see well in darkness. 'Have sharp night eyes' is a literal and unnatural compound.

highlights.text: I have sharp night eyes, but for some reason I absolutely can't see.

adjudicated.jp: 人類が消えてしまった今、その程度の不思議現象は気にする価値もない。
adjudicated.en: In the present, where humanity has vanished, an inexplicable phenomenon of this level isn't worth paying attention to.
comments: I suspect Tanaka was just trying to see how much troll he could get away with by simply stating "don't worry about it" right afterwards. Since everyone seems worried about the origins of the loop or the nature of the parallel world, and no one seems to question Taichi's beat-you-over-the-head preposterous explanation of his night vision or whatever's going on here, it seems the answer is clear. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 中に入る。
adjudicated.en: I go inside.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 当然のように、鎧とかが置いてある。
adjudicated.en: Naturally, there is a suit of armor inside.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ……のかも知れないが、窓が締め切ってあるから真っ暗だ。
adjudicated.en: ...or so I sort of guess, because it's pitch-black darkness due to the windows being firmly shut.
comments: See CCD1001. So is Misato's house. How odd. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: これではいくら夜目がきいても、視界は確保できない。
adjudicated.en: With things like this, no matter how sharp my night vision, I can't be certain of what I see.
comments: The experiment extends afterwards, too. Theory: he's not outside of school, he's not seeing anything because there's nothing to see, Touko's not dead but in the infirmary passed out due to lack of food, Taichi's hallucinating everything including her death... and also it avoids having to have BGs of the inside of the mansion, so there's a tech troll as well. See CCC3018, end. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Even excellent night vision cannot secure any visibility in total darkness. The English instead says that he cannot be certain about what he does see.

highlights.text: With things like this, no matter how sharp my night vision, I can't be certain of what I see.

adjudicated.jp: 屋敷をうろつきまわる。
adjudicated.en: I wander through the residence.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 迷路のようだった。
adjudicated.en: It was like a maze.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子の部屋はどこだろう。
adjudicated.en: Where could Touko's room even be.
comments: Why, exactly where he knows it is, since he's come here before! Ah, right, he doesn't remember yet, see see CCC4015 when he will. Troll troll. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 二階かな。
adjudicated.en: Second floor maybe?
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 階段をのぼる。
adjudicated.en: I climb the staircase.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: なんかゾンビが出そうな屋敷だなあ。
adjudicated.en: This is the kind of a mansion where you'd just see some zombies popping out, isn't it.
comments: As long as it's not Chris's blood, we'll be safe. See CCB2010. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 'The kind of a mansion' incorrectly combines the definite construction 'the kind of' with an indefinite article.

highlights.text: This is the kind of a mansion where you'd just see some zombies popping out, isn't it.

adjudicated.jp: 「冬子ー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "TOUKOOO!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 返事はない。
adjudicated.en: No response.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 声は屋敷の豪奢な絨毯に、吸い取られてしまう。
adjudicated.en: The mansion's luxurious runner carpets completely absorb my voice.
comments: How does he see them??? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 部屋を一つ一つ確認していく。
adjudicated.en: I go check the rooms one by one.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 面倒。
adjudicated.en: What a pain.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ……曜子ちゃんについてきてもらえばよかった。
adjudicated.en: ...it'd have been better if I had come with Youko-chan.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi wishes that he had asked Youko to come along with him. 'If I had come with Youko' reverses who would be accompanying whom.

highlights.text: ...it'd have been better if I had come with Youko-chan.

adjudicated.jp: と、無数にある扉の一つを開くと。
adjudicated.en: So, I open one of the countless doors there.
comments: Just at random, and boom, got it? This is too blatant to be a plot hole. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 光がさしこんだ。
adjudicated.en: Light was shining in.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 窓は全開だった。
adjudicated.en: The window was wide open.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そっと入り込んだ風が、室内を旋回してまた出ていく。
adjudicated.en: The wind gently enters, makes the rounds of the room's interior, then leaves.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: だからだろうか。
adjudicated.en: This is probably why,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 腐臭さえしない。
adjudicated.en: there's no smell of rot.
comments: No, it's because there's no insects... in part because he doesn't "know" this, in part to keep the troll that Touko is, indeed, just sleeping. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...Touko."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 触れる気がしなかった。
adjudicated.en: I did not feel like touching her.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 嫌悪感ではない。
adjudicated.en: Not because of revulsion.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: その有様が、尊く思えたからだ。
adjudicated.en: Because this state seemed, to me, sacred.
comments: Because she'd wake up. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 眠り姫を思わせて、気高い。
adjudicated.en: A nobility that reminded me of Sleeping Beauty.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that the sight evokes Sleeping Beauty and is noble. The English turns the predicate into the fragment 'A nobility.'

highlights.text: A nobility that reminded me of Sleeping Beauty.

adjudicated.jp: 群青の冬子は一人だった。
adjudicated.en: Touko the Ultramarine of Gunjou was alone.
adjudicated.assessment: 群青 is the institution or group name Gunjou in this construction. 'Touko the Ultramarine of Gunjou' translates the same name twice and invents an epithet.

highlights.text: Touko the Ultramarine of Gunjou was alone.

adjudicated.jp: もとはお嬢様学校に通っていた。
adjudicated.en: Originally, she went to a rich ladies' school.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 適応係数調査試験で弾かれて、ここに来た。
adjudicated.en: Plucked off by the Conformity Coefficient Test, she came here.
adjudicated.assessment: The test rejected or screened Touko out. 'Plucked off' describes removal by picking and is not the social or evaluative rejection expressed here.

highlights.text: Plucked off by the Conformity Coefficient Test, she came here.

adjudicated.jp: ……屋敷ごと。
adjudicated.en: ...together with the mansion.
comments: This is confirmed even later, they moved the Kirihara Mansion to be here for Touko. Via train. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 適応係数は百分比で表される。
adjudicated.en: The Conformity Coefficient is represented with a percentage.
adjudicated.assessment: A value is expressed 'as a percentage,' not 'with a percentage.'

highlights.text: The Conformity Coefficient is represented with a percentage.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子は４６。
adjudicated.en: Touko's 46.
comments: Hum, with Tomoki's 17 and Sakuraba's 15, that's 78. I got nothing else. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 群青では、高からず低からず。
adjudicated.en: In Gunjou, neither the highest nor the lowest.
adjudicated.assessment: Her value is neither high nor low within Gunjou. 'Neither the highest nor the lowest' merely denies the two extreme ranks and allows a value that is still high or low.

highlights.text: In Gunjou, neither the highest nor the lowest.

adjudicated.jp: 乱暴なものの見方をすれば、半分は普通だったと言える。
adjudicated.en: If we look at this rudely, it could be said that she's halfway normal.
comments: Seems more rude than blunt here... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 会話を拒絶した。教師に対しても。
adjudicated.en: She refused conversation. Even with the teachers.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 学校に来ても制服を拒み、内にこもって人を拒み。
adjudicated.en: She came to school but refused the uniform, she segregates herself inside and rejects the people.
comments: Inside the classroom, not inside herself... though there's not much difference. And of course, when she says "people grew thin until they disappeared", she doesn't mean that everybody has physically disappeared; just that they've dumped her and left alone. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She shut herself away and rejected people. 'Segregates herself inside' is unidiomatic, changes tense, and does not express withdrawal into herself or her room.

highlights.text: She came to school but refused the uniform, she segregates herself inside and rejects the people.

adjudicated.jp: どこにも属さず誰にもへつらわず。
adjudicated.en: Belonging nowhere, being nice to no one.
adjudicated.assessment: へつらう means to flatter, fawn, or curry favor. 'Being nice to no one' wrongly turns refusal to abase herself into a lack of ordinary kindness.

highlights.text: Belonging nowhere, being nice to no one.

adjudicated.jp: けれど心の中は、人への渇望で揺れていた。
adjudicated.en: But, inside her heart, she was swaying with a longing for people.
comments: See CCA0013, CCX0001. We're meant to read that innocently, then nastily, then... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: だから俺は、すぐに惹かれてしまった。
adjudicated.en: And that is why I was, immediately, completely, charmed.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そして今、冬子は寝台の上で小ぎれいに手を組んでいる。
adjudicated.en: And now, Touko is laying on top of her bed, her hands neatly overlapped.
adjudicated.assessment: A person lies on a bed; 'is laying' is transitive and requires an object.

highlights.text: And now, Touko is laying on top of her bed, her hands neatly overlapped.

adjudicated.jp: 自分でそうしたのだろうか。
adjudicated.en: She probably did that on her own.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator wonders whether she arranged herself that way. The English turns the question into a probability assertion.

highlights.text: She probably did that on her own.

adjudicated.jp: 眠るように去ったのだろうか。
adjudicated.en: She probably passed as if sleeping.
comments: Notice how he never actually checks the corpse for a pulse. Now notice how he never even THINKS to check the corpse for a pulse. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator wonders whether she departed as if falling asleep. The English asserts probability and uses the incomplete verb 'passed' instead of preserving the question.

highlights.text: She probably passed as if sleeping.

adjudicated.jp: きっと、そうなのだ。
adjudicated.en: I'm sure, she must have.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 悲劇的な結末だとは思う。一般的には。
adjudicated.en: This looks like a tragic conclusion. Typically it would be.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: けど悲しささえ圧倒的な尊厳に塗りかえられて。
adjudicated.en: But even the sadness is varnished with an overwhelming sense of dignity.
adjudicated.assessment: Overwhelming dignity overwrites even the sadness. 'Varnished with' merely coats sadness and reverses which element transforms the other.

highlights.text: But even the sadness is varnished with an overwhelming sense of dignity.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は感動し、佇んだ。
adjudicated.en: Moved, I stand still.
comments: Oh, another one of those that work so well in English. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrative reports that he was moved and stood there. The English unexpectedly switches to present tense.

highlights.text: Moved, I stand still.

adjudicated.jp: 「……そうか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...well then."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 一人で去った。
adjudicated.en: She left us, alone.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: あの冬子が……一人で。
adjudicated.en: Touko went... alone.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「やるな……冬子」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You did it... Touko."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 衰弱か。薬か。餓えか。
adjudicated.en: Debilitation? Drugs? Starvation?
comments: She's probably sedated via drugs because of debilitation via starvation. Who needs lies when you have truth like this? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: それはわからない。
adjudicated.en: I have no idea of what.
adjudicated.assessment: He does not know which of the preceding causes applies. 'I have no idea of what' is incomplete and does not point back to the alternatives.

highlights.text: I have no idea of what.

adjudicated.jp: 暴く気もない。
adjudicated.en: Finding out, unthinkable.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi has no intention of uncovering the cause. 'Finding out, unthinkable' changes lack of intent into a moral or conceptual impossibility.

highlights.text: Finding out, unthinkable.

adjudicated.jp: 一つ言えること。
adjudicated.en: There's one thing that can be said:
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 天蓋つきの寝台に抱かれ、時を止めたように横たわる冬子の様は、夢と現実のあわいを感じさせて幻想的だった。
adjudicated.en: Touko laying down as if time itself had stopped, embraced in this canopied bed, was a thing of fairy tale that made me feel the boundary between dream and reality.
comments: See CCA0001. One ought wonder, at this point, whether Youko isn't a post-facto fictional character based on all the characters around him, for starters, on Touko herself. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 祝福を。
adjudicated.en: I give my blessing,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 扉を閉める。
adjudicated.en: and close the door.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 闇に一人。
adjudicated.en: Alone in the dark.
comments: Ah, great, Resident Evil wasn't enough so we're going to the source now? This is almost too perfect to be coincidental. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 屋敷を出ることにした。
adjudicated.en: I decided to leave the mansion.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: リセットが発生すれば、また彼女に会える。
adjudicated.en: If the reset happens, I will see her once more.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: その事実が脳裏に呼び覚まされたのは、屋敷を出る直前だった。
adjudicated.en: That fact woke up in my mind just before I left the mansion.
adjudicated.assessment: The fact came back to mind. It did not literally 'wake up in' his mind.

highlights.text: That fact woke up in my mind just before I left the mansion.

adjudicated.jp: 尊さも、繰り返されれば輝きを失う。
adjudicated.en: Even what is sacred loses its radiance if it is repeated.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子の決意とか、寂しさとか、闘争とか。
adjudicated.en: Touko's determination, Touko's loneliness, Touko's struggles, everything.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ……イライラした。
adjudicated.en: ...that pissed me off.
comments: See CCC3019A. Never a coincidence here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 汚されたように感じた。
adjudicated.en: It felt as if she was being dirtied.
adjudicated.assessment: He feels as if the sacred moment or its dignity has been defiled. The English instead says that Touko herself is being dirtied.

highlights.text: It felt as if she was being dirtied.

adjudicated.jp: じゃあ、俺は何のために……
adjudicated.en: Then, for what purpose did I...
comments: supposing "...dump her" -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子を突き放したのだろう。
adjudicated.en: To get away from Touko, that's why.
adjudicated.assessment: Together with the preceding line, this asks why he had pushed Touko away. The English turns the second half into the answer 'To get away from Touko, that's why.'

highlights.text: To get away from Touko, that's why.

adjudicated.jp: 帰りの車でも、イライラは消えなかった。
adjudicated.en: Even on the ride back, my irritation did not vanish.
comments: Kiri is being bullied by Youko, and Touko has died. (Even if Youko doesn't exist and Touko hasn't died.) See CCC0000, CCC3018: as if paramnesia, the pattern will now repeat again. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

withheld.jp: 孤高でいる時の冬子は、誇りと屈辱にまみれて……キレイだった。
withheld.en: When she stands above all others, Touko is smeared in pride and disgrace... she was so beautiful.
comments: See Youko. A random CR was removed in the console version. -GHS
